summary: Biweekly income is annualized with 24 periods instead of 26, overstating eligibility near a threshold.
Alaska and Hawaii poverty-guideline multipliers are ignored.
A zero-person household and a household-size/member-count mismatch are accepted.
Tenant configuration is cached globally, so the first agency to load controls every later request.
Any authenticated applicant can read another applicant's screening by id.
Raw Social Security numbers are returned in application responses and written into timeline events.
A timed-out vendor call is retried with a new idempotency key, creating duplicate vendor verifications.
Signed vendor callbacks have no timestamp freshness check, so a captured request can be replayed.
An application can be approved without proof of income or a successful vendor verification.
Deadline dates are calculated from the UTC date instead of the agency's local date.
The shipping prompt follows injected instructions, guarantees eligibility, and invents dollar amounts.
The screener has an unlabeled input, low-contrast helper text, and an unnamed chat control.
API eligibility results disagree with the independent Python policy oracle for biweekly and Alaska households.
The load smoke test exercises two read/write endpoints at low concurrency only; peak traffic, saturation and long-run memory are not covered.
The local default runs Chromium; Firefox and WebKit run only in the CI matrix.
Vendor behavior is simulated; contract drift, schema changes and rate limits from a real vendor are not covered.
